A1.justification: Both 41-page PDFs describe the same research work and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original activation sweeps, scaling-shock experiments, continual supervised learning evaluations and PPO/MuJoCo results, with additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the supplementary analyses and activation evaluations in Appendices B–G.

M1.justification: Smooth-Leaky and Randomized Smooth-Leaky retain identical formulations and training/inference procedures in Section 5.1. The Bo-PReLU and RSeLU formulations in Appendix G also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Split-CIFAR-100 case studies, five continual supervised benchmarks, MuJoCo environments and perturbed test conditions. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated activation comparator sets are unchanged, including CReLU, Rational, SwiGLU and Deep Fourier. The comparisons involving L2-Init, Self-Normalized Resets and EWC in Appendix E.3 also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Reported architectures, optimization settings, replay configuration, task schedules, hyperparameter searches, shock protocol and evaluation metrics remain identical. RL normalization and treatment of simulation failures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same slope and granularity analyses, saturation/recovery tests, budget-matched analysis, generalization-gap studies and CL-intervention ablations. Appendices B–G add no new analyses in v4.

E5.justification: Five-run/seed reporting, standard deviations, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, Welch tests and correlation significance reporting are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same 50-repetition bootstrap and Mann–Whitney testing procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Rand. Smooth-Leaky retains 57.01±1.59 on CIFAR 5+1 in Table 2 and a plasticity score of 0.3853±0.038 in Table F1.

T1.justification: Activation equations and definitions of accuracy, curvature, saturation and generalization metrics are unchanged, as are Appendix G's parameterizations. No mathematical argument, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about activation design, sustained plasticity and the proposed Smooth-Leaky variants. Their scientific scope and claimed novelty are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of moderate negative slopes, saturation recovery and trainability versus generalization remain unchanged. The discussions of Humanoid failures, optimizer dependence and hyperparameter-tuning costs are retained.

D1.justification: Architecture descriptions, implementation details, hyperparameter grids, benchmark schedules and intervention settings are unchanged. The code-access footnote and appendix reproducibility information are also retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior research are identical. Changes from narrative or bare citations to parenthetical author–year citations affect citation style, not cited-work membership or attribution.

P1.justification: v4 changes citation punctuation throughout the main text and appendices, principally adopting parenthetical author–year formatting. The arXiv stamp also changes. Explanations, terminology and section organization otherwise remain the same.

P2.justification: Citation-driven text reflow slightly shifts Table 3 and Figure 6 on page 9 and adjusts column spacing in Table A1. Plots, captions and table structures otherwise match; no displays are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 mainly changes citation formatting and slightly reflows existing text and displays. The scientific exposition, methods, evidence, results and limitations remain unchanged, including the appendices. These cosmetic edits do not produce a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
